name: IntuneStatefulDeviceFingerprinting
description: KuShu-Shimon Intune Stateful Device Fingerprinting (ISDF) provides a tamper-resistant device fingerprint for enrolled Windows devices, enforced via Intune Custom Compliance and DPAPI-encrypted baselines. In Cloud mode it attests fingerprints to Entra ID through APIM and a Logic App to enable trusted device filters, dynamic groups, and stronger Conditional Access policies. The solution collects on-device signals, stores encrypted baselines, self-heals missing keys, and reports ISDF booleans for compliant state.
author: Graham Hild

securityCheck.aiSummary: Overall, the IntuneStatefulDeviceFingerprinting code includes legitimate admin telemetry and compliance features, but it exhibits obfuscation, persistence mechanisms, and outbound telemetry that warrant strong governance. Recommendations: replace EncodedCommand usage with signed, auditable scripts; document and control the scheduled task (scope, duration, and logging); ensure webhook endpoints are trusted and data minimization is applied; explicit error logging; verify certificate handling with least privilege and secure storage; and consider opt-in/transparent telemetry controls to reduce risk of unintended data exposure.
